To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermal expansion of Hume-Rothery solutions is a linear function of the electroresistivity.

in the electron solutions of Cu-Zn, in addition to the usual temperature dependence of electroresistance, there is an additional component, which is a consequence of the temperature dependence of the thermal deformation.
the electroresistance of electron solutions based Cu and Zn increases with temperature and decreases with increasing electron concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the structure of the electron solution and the nature of the charge carriers on the properties of the phase.
the study of the influence of the electron structure of the Hume-Rothery solutions based on copper and the zinc on the electroresistance of these solutions.
the possibility of using the electroresistance of electron solutions for the development of thermoresistive elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electroresistance of electron solutions is determined by the electron density, and the thermal expansion of electron solution is determined by the concentration of the alloying element and the electron density.
the electroresistance is a thermodynamic property of electron solutions.
, in general, the electroresistance is not a thermodynamic property of the electron solutions, but is determined by the properties of the electron gas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron solution of the Cu-Zn system is a thermodynamically stable system with a high level of structural and physical perfection.
the electroresistance is the main factor determining the thermal deformation of electron solution phases.

, for the first time in the literature, the temperature dependence of the thermal deformation and electroresistance of electron solutions (phases of the Hume-Rothery type) based on Cu and CuZn alloys was studied in situ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electroresistance of electron solutions based of Cu and Zn is a function of the thermal expansion coefficient.
the thermal expansion and electroresistance of electron solutions can be used for a quantitative assessment of the degree of structural disordering.
the thermal expansion and the electroresistance of electron solutions are interrelated and that the thermal expansion coefficient is proportional to the square of the electroresistant coefficient.
